ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A cylindrical oil tank is partially filled with oil, with its cross-section shown in the figure. It is known that the radius of the cross-section $\odot O$ is $5\,\text{cm}$, and the width of the oil surface $AB$ is $6\,\text{cm}$. If more oil is added into the tank, and the width of the oil surface becomes $8\,\text{cm}$, by how many centimeters does the oil surface $AB$ rise?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve in two cases:\\
(1) As shown in Figure 1, for the oil surface CD with a width of 8cm, draw $ON\perp AB$ intersecting CD and AB at points M and N respectively.\\
From the problem statement, we know\\
$OM\perp CD$,\\
$CM=MD=\frac{1}{2}CD=4\,\text{cm}$,\\
$AN=BN=\frac{1}{2}AB=3\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle BON$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$ON=\sqrt{OB^{2}-BN^{2}}=4\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle DOM$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$OM=\sqrt{OD^{2}-DM^{2}}=3\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore MN=ON-OM=1\,\text{cm}$\\
(2) As shown in Figure 2, for the oil surface EF with a width of 8cm, draw $PN\perp EF$ intersecting AB and EF at points N and P respectively, and connect OB.\\
From the problem statement, we know\\
$PN\perp AB$,\\
$EP=PF=\frac{1}{2}EF=4\,\text{cm}$,\\
$AN=BN=\frac{1}{2}AB=3\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle BON$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$ON=\sqrt{OB^{2}-BN^{2}}=4\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle EPO$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$OP=\sqrt{OE^{2}-EP^{2}}=3\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore NP=ON+OP=7\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore$ The oil surface AB rises to CD by 1cm, and the oil surface AB rises to EF by \boxed{7}cm;

当油面宽度变为 8 cm 时，新水平弦的一半为 4 cm，所以圆心到该弦的距离为 sqrt(5^2-4^2)=sqrt(25-16)=3 cm。宽度为 8 cm 的水平弦可能在圆心下方 3 cm，也可能在圆心上方 3 cm。

若新油面在 O 下方 3 cm，则油面从 O 下方 4 cm 上升到 O 下方 3 cm，上升 4-3=1 cm。若新油面在 O 上方 3 cm，则油面从 O 下方 4 cm 上升到 O 上方 3 cm，上升 4+3=7 cm。

raw_record.original_question: A cylindrical oil tank is partially filled with oil, with its cross-section shown in the figure. It is known that the radius of the cross-section $\odot O$ is $5\,\text{cm}$, and the width of the oil surface $AB$ is $6\,\text{cm}$. If more oil is added into the tank, and the width of the oil surface becomes $8\,\text{cm}$, by how many centimeters does the oil surface $AB$ rise?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve in two cases:\\
(1) As shown in Figure 1, for the oil surface CD with a width of 8cm, draw $ON\perp AB$ intersecting CD and AB at points M and N respectively.\\
From the problem statement, we know\\
$OM\perp CD$,\\
$CM=MD=\frac{1}{2}CD=4\,\text{cm}$,\\
$AN=BN=\frac{1}{2}AB=3\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle BON$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$ON=\sqrt{OB^{2}-BN^{2}}=4\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle DOM$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$OM=\sqrt{OD^{2}-DM^{2}}=3\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore MN=ON-OM=1\,\text{cm}$\\
(2) As shown in Figure 2, for the oil surface EF with a width of 8cm, draw $PN\perp EF$ intersecting AB and EF at points N and P respectively, and connect OB.\\
From the problem statement, we know\\
$PN\perp AB$,\\
$EP=PF=\frac{1}{2}EF=4\,\text{cm}$,\\
$AN=BN=\frac{1}{2}AB=3\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle BON$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$ON=\sqrt{OB^{2}-BN^{2}}=4\,\text{cm}$\\
In $\triangle EPO$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have\\
$OP=\sqrt{OE^{2}-EP^{2}}=3\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore NP=ON+OP=7\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore$ The oil surface AB rises to CD by 1cm, and the oil surface AB rises to EF by \boxed{7}cm;

Image description: In the figure there is a circular cross-section, and the center of the circle is marked as O; near the bottom there is a horizontal chord AB, and the small circular arc region below AB is indicated by slanted shading as oil, so the current oil surface is the horizontal chord AB near the bottom, and after adding oil the oil surface moves upward.

Reasoning: The radius r=5 cm, and the initial oil surface AB=6 cm. Draw the perpendicular from the center O to chord AB. According to the perpendicular diameter theorem, half of AB is 3 cm, so the distance from the center to AB is sqrt(5^2-3^2)=sqrt(25-9)=4 cm. Since AB is below the center, the initial oil surface position can be regarded as 4 cm below O.

When the oil surface width becomes 8 cm, half of the new horizontal chord is 4 cm, so the distance from the center to this chord is sqrt(5^2-4^2)=sqrt(25-16)=3 cm. A horizontal chord with width 8 cm may be 3 cm below the center, or may be 3 cm above the center.

If the new oil surface is 3 cm below O, then the oil surface rises from 4 cm below O to 3 cm below O, rising 4-3=1 cm. If the new oil surface is 3 cm above O, then the oil surface rises from 4 cm below O to 3 cm above O, rising 4+3=7 cm.
